notes: Majiayao culture of the upper Yellow River, a Neolithic culture of Gansu and eastern Qinghai (the brief's horizon is 3400 BCE, so its whole life starts inside the range). Infobox 'c. 3300 - c. 2000 BC', 'Geographical range: upper Yellow River'; 'It is often split into Majiayao (3300-2500 BC), Banshan (2500-2300 BC) and Machang (2300-2000 BC)'; 'Preceded by: Yangshao culture (5000-3000 BC)', 'Followed by: Qijia culture'. One passage of the page gives '3000-2000 BC', in conflict with 3300. Extent: 'The core area is eastern Gansu', Majiayao-phase sites 'along the upper Wei, upper Bailong, and middle and lower Tao and Daxia valleys, plus the lower Datong River', 'eastern Qinghai' and 'northern Sichuan' (extent not stated), type site near Majiayao village in Lintao County; the Tianshui disc without Guanzhong (the Yangshao's former Gansu disc), Lanzhou (110 km), Linxia (80 km, the Tao and Daxia valleys) and Xining (100 km, the Huangshui) are drawn, confidence 2; northern Sichuan and the Bailong are not drawn. The Hexi Corridor and Xinjiang are routes of influence ('Pottery style spread to Xinjiang and Central Asia') and not drawn. Succession: the Yangshao is the predecessor ('developed from the middle Yangshao (Miaodigou) phase' through the Shilingxia phase); 'Qijia succeeded Majiayao at the end of the 3rd millennium BC' and 'later occupied western Gansu and eastern Qinghai'; no dossier for the Qijia yet (counterpart), whose dates are not on this page. The oldest bronze knife (2900-2740 BC) and Machang copper objects are not territory. No area figure.
